html:
The War of the Pacific was fought from 1879 to 1884 between Chile and the allied countries of Peru and Bolivia, over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Chile won and took the coastal provinces of both.

In 1878 Bolivia raised taxes on a Chilean nitrate company at Antofagasta, breaking a treaty. When Bolivia moved to seize it, Chile occupied the port in February 1879. Peru, bound by a secret alliance, was drawn in. At sea, the Peruvian ironclad Huáscar held out for months, and the Chilean captain Arturo Prat died at Iquique and became a national hero. Chile then invaded Peru and occupied Lima in 1881.

Chile gained the nitrate fields of Tarapacá and Antofagasta, the base of its nitrate boom. Bolivia lost its coast, a loss it still mourns, which shaped the Chaco War and the gas war. Peru lost a province and much of its pride.
sum: The War of the Pacific was fought from 1879 to 1884 between Chile and the allied countries of Peru and Bolivia, over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Chile won and took the coastal provinces of both.
